questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the difference between latency and throughput?

options.text: Latency is requests per second; throughput is time per request
Latency is how long one request takes; throughput is how many requests complete per unit of time
They are two names for the same measurement
Latency applies to reads; throughput applies to writes

questions.explanation: Latency is per-request time; throughput is volume over time. Adding parallel workers can raise throughput without changing per-request latency.

questions.prompt: Why do engineers report p99 latency instead of the average?

options.text: The average is harder to compute
p99 is always smaller, so it looks better
The average hides the slow tail that real users experience

questions.explanation: A few very slow requests drag the average in a misleading way. p99 shows what the slowest 1% of requests actually experience.

questions.prompt: Approximately how much downtime per year does 99.99% availability (four nines) allow?
questions.explanation: Four nines allows roughly 52.6 minutes of downtime per year. Three nines is ~8.8 hours; five nines is ~5.3 minutes.

questions.prompt: Match each reliability term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A measured indicator of service quality
The internal target for an indicator
The amount of failure the SLO permits

questions.explanation: The SLI is measured, the SLO is the target you hold it to, the SLA is the contractual promise (usually looser than the SLO), and the error budget is 100% minus the SLO.

questions.prompt: Which are true of scaling out (horizontal scaling)? Select all that apply.

options.text: It spreads load across more machines
It can be made fault-tolerant with no single machine as a hard ceiling
It always guarantees strong consistency for free

questions.explanation: Scaling out adds machines, avoids a single-machine ceiling, and can be fault-tolerant — but it brings distributed-systems challenges. Consistency is not free; it is one of those challenges.

questions.prompt: If your SLO is 99.9% success, the 0.1% of allowed failure is called your ______ ______. (two words)
questions.explanation: The error budget is 100% minus the SLO — the amount of failure you are allowed to spend on risk and change.
